items.title: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 (Cth)
items.version: Compilation No. 39, compilation date 28 March 2026, register ID C2026C00117, Authorised Version registered 1 April 2026; marked latest and current on the Federal Register of Legislation on 2026-10-02
items.licence: CC BY 4.0, Federal Register of Legislation terms of use (https://www.legislation.gov.au/terms-of-use: all content except the Coat of Arms and where otherwise noted); the PDF carries no notice of its own. Attribution: 'Sourced from the Federal Register of Legislation at 2 October 2026. For the latest information on Australian Government law please go to https://www.legislation.gov.au.'
items.why: default rules for every Act and, through the Legislation Act, every legislative instrument: definitions (s 2B), commencement of Acts (s 3A), the effect of repeal and amendment, what counts as part of an Act, purposive interpretation and extrinsic material (ss 15AA, 15AB), appointment, acting and delegation (ss 33-34A, including ss 34AA and 34AB), service, and time, distance and age (including s 37A); the most important item in the set

items.why: the Federal Register of Legislation, compilations and authorised versions (Chapter 2), what a legislative or notifiable instrument is (Chapter 1 Part 2), drafting standards and consultation (Chapter 3 Part 1), tabling and disallowance (Chapter 3 Part 2), automatic repeal of spent instruments and provisions (Chapter 3 Part 3, ss 48A-48E), and sunsetting (Chapter 3 Part 4); when and how a subject's delegated legislation takes effect, can be disallowed, and ceases

items.title: Legislation (Exemptions and Other Matters) Regulation 2015 (Cth)
items.version: Compilation No. 24, compilation date 22 January 2026, register ID F2026C00064, Authorised Version registered 22 January 2026; marked latest and current on the Federal Register of Legislation on 2026-10-02
items.licence: CC BY 4.0, Federal Register of Legislation terms of use (https://www.legislation.gov.au/terms-of-use); the PDF carries no notice of its own. Attribution: 'Sourced from the Federal Register of Legislation at 2 October 2026. For the latest information on Australian Government law please go to https://www.legislation.gov.au.'
items.why: the Legislation Act cannot be applied to a given instrument without it: it lists the classes of instruments that are not legislative instruments (s 6), the notifiable instruments (Part 3), and the instruments exempt from disallowance and from sunsetting; whether a subject's delegated legislation can be disallowed or sunsets is decided here

items.title: Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth), Volume 1 (sections 1-5 and Schedule sections 1.1-261.3), for Chapter 2 of the Criminal Code
items.version: Compilation No. 174, compilation date 30 June 2026, register ID C2026C00243, Authorised Version registered 30 June 2026, Volume 1 of 3; marked latest and current on the Federal Register of Legislation on 2026-10-02 (the register gives this version an end date of 26 February 2027, a scheduled self-repeal, so it will be superseded then)
items.licence: CC BY 4.0, Federal Register of Legislation terms of use (https://www.legislation.gov.au/terms-of-use); the PDF carries no notice of its own. Attribution: 'Sourced from the Federal Register of Legislation at 2 October 2026. For the latest information on Australian Government law please go to https://www.legislation.gov.au.'
items.why: Chapter 2 (general principles of criminal responsibility: physical and fault elements, default fault elements in s 5.6, strict and absolute liability in ss 6.1-6.2, defences, extensions of liability, geographical jurisdiction, corporate criminal responsibility) applies to every offence against a law of the Commonwealth (s 2.2(2)); only Volume 1 is pinned because Chapter 2 is wholly in it, and the rest of the Code is offences, not meta-legislation

items.title: Crimes Act 1914 (Cth), Volume 1 (Parts I to IA, sections 1-15F), for the general penalty and prosecution rules in Part IA
items.version: Compilation No. 167, compilation date 27 August 2026, register ID C2026C00368, Authorised Version registered 2 September 2026, Volume 1 of 3; marked latest and current on the Federal Register of Legislation on 2026-10-02
items.licence: CC BY 4.0, Federal Register of Legislation terms of use (https://www.legislation.gov.au/terms-of-use); the PDF carries no notice of its own. Attribution: 'Sourced from the Federal Register of Legislation at 2 October 2026. For the latest information on Australian Government law please go to https://www.legislation.gov.au.'
items.why: the general penalty rules every Commonwealth offence relies on: the value of a penalty unit (s 4AA), pecuniary penalties for natural persons and bodies corporate, including conversion of imprisonment to a fine (s 4B), continuing and multiple offences (s 4K), and time for commencement of prosecutions (s 15B); Commonwealth Acts state penalties in penalty units and leave these rules to the Crimes Act; only Volume 1 is pinned because these provisions are wholly in it
